text.p: Leading stories in the Greek press:
ELEFTHEROTYPIA
--Prime Minister and PASOK leader Costas Simitis explains the dilemma facing Greek voters. "This law allows only one winner," Simitis says. "Votes for smaller parties favour a New Democracy win".
--The scheduled no-show of former premier and New Democracy honorary president Constantine Mitsotakis a major factor in Miltiades Evert's decision to call off ND's Athens rally.
--The Left Coalition holds its best-ever rally in Athens. Leader Nikos Constantopoulos stresses that all political trends must be represented in Parliament.
--Political Spring's Andonis Samaras predicts the creation of a new political scene after the elections
--Communists: "The 'centre-left' is a myth".
ELEFTHEROS TYPOS

--Bold decision by New Democracy leader Miltiades Evert to cancel Thursday's planned party rally in Athens. Evert chooses dialogue over Athens fiesta. Confident of victory following yesterday's rallies. "On Sunday, Greece will be in the hands of the people," he says.

--Simitis and his cynical confession: The armed forces will not ever return to the islet of Imia. ND deputy president Ioannis Varvitsiotis poses 10 questions over the government's handling of the crisis between Greece and Turkey in late January.
ETHNOS
--Former premier Constantine Mitsotakis the one who brought Evert "off the balcony" by refusing to stand beside his successor to the ND leadership at the party's planned Athens rally on Thursday.
--Straight answers on the economy, society and national issues from Prime Minister and PASOK leader Costas Simitis in his interview last night.
TA NEA
--New Democracy looks to ensure victory by launching a dirty war on Simitis.
--PASOK's 'big guns' for the final stretch to victory: Athens rally, bringing Democratic Social Movement supporters back to the fold and a barrage on radio and television.
--DHKKI's president Tsovolas to sue following claims by Athens daily that his holiday home was illegally built.
KATHIMERINI
--Evert's bold - if risky - manoeuvres. Main opposition leader calls off traditional New Democracy rally in Athens' city centre and proposes TV dialogue with all parties.
--Simitis comes across as prudent and realistic in the crucial area of the economy in last night's television interview.
--Increased university entrances "nothing to do with elections", Education Minister George Papandreou says.
--Thousands rally for Left Coalition in Athens last night: "Next Sunday night, the Coalition's absence from the Parliament will end," leader Nikos Constantopoulos says.
--Changes to tax code in the offing. New code aims at streamlining procedures and introducing electronic data interchange.
--Candidates vie to become (OTE) telecommunications organisation partner to hold 25 percent and play management role in new subsidiary developing DCS 1800 system.
--Natural gas project ready to go into operation, DEPA says
--National Bank of Greece estimates 10 billion drachma profit from foreign activity this year.
--Central bank moves successfully to protect drachma from speculators.
IMERISIA
--Optimistic message from Athens bourse, price index closes at close to 1000 points.
--New estimates put forecast 1996 inflation at 8.1 percent. Downward trend to continue this month. Fuel prices will be critical for consumer price index.
--Simitis: the injustices of 'objective tax criteria' will be removed.
--Federation of Greek Exporters calls on new government to give Greek exports a push with five-point plan, including improving international transit and telecommunications links.
EXPRESS

--To the point: Party finance ministers speak to Express. Anti-inflationary policies must not change - lower interest rates a lever for investment activity, National Economy Minister Yiannos Papandoniou says. Speed up privatisation and get private sector to participate in major public works projects, counters former New Democracy economy minister Stephanos Manos.
--59 percent of all mutual fund capital invested in state titles.
KERDOS
--Lively interest in bank shares in yesterday's trading. General index closes at 974 points.
--Markets keep their distance from election tension. Interest centres on developments after the Sunday poll, bank sources say.
NAFTEMBORIKI
--Simitis pledges no new taxes in 1997 state budget
--Bank of Greece pressures for secondary bonds market. Legislative framework for modernisation of capital market ready.
--Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
